stories.title: Graphene measurements reveal energy-loss and quantum-coherence exponents diverge under gate control
stories.desc: Scientists have shown that the two exponents (inelastic scattering exponent and dephasing exponent) commonly used to describe electron scattering in graphene do not necessarily follow the same behavior. Using gated epitaxial graphene, a multi-institutional team of researchers independently…

stories.title: Pigeons' proposed inner-ear compass runs into a noise problem
stories.desc: A pigeon turning its head might seem an unlikely electricity generator. Yet one proposed explanation for the bird's magnetic sense depends on exactly that: Turning through Earth's magnetic field would produce tiny electrical signals inside its ears. However, a theoretical study suggests that this…

stories.title: Scientists build world's most accurate atomic clock
stories.desc: Take a second and turn it into trillions of moments. Measure each one. That's how precisely an atomic clock at Singapore's Centre for Quantum Technologies (CQT) keeps time—and with record-setting accuracy, according to results published in Nature on Sept. 23.

stories.title: Quantum device simulates matter popping into existence
stories.desc: A research team led by faculty at the Duke Quantum Center (DQC) has observed string-breaking dynamics related to particle-antiparticle formation on a quantum simulator, among the first such observations in quantum physics.

stories.title: Biology Might Not Be Quantum, but Its Math Is Quantumlike
stories.desc: Scientists have a history of trying — and failing — to link biology and quantum mechanics. The real connection between them may be in the math. The post Biology Might Not Be Quantum, but Its Math Is Quantumlike first appeared on Quanta Magazine

stories.title: Could negative mass exist and be observed?
stories.desc: Unlike electric charge, as far as we know all mass is positive, and positive masses attract one another. Could negative mass exist, and if so, what would be the ramifications?

stories.title: Central surface density of dark matter agrees with the prediction of a new theory of gravity
stories.desc: A researcher from Sejong University has used a new theory of gravity proposed by Erik Verlinde to predict the observed central surface density of dark matter. The study was published in Physics of the Dark Universe on Sept. 20.

stories.title: Making Sense of Shallow-Water Waves with Advanced Statistics
stories.desc: Low-frequency infragravity waves shape shorelines, but exactly how they contribute is mysterious. A technique from Bayesian probability theory might change that.

stories.title: Cloudy Cloak Over the Northwest
stories.desc: A low-lying cloud layer brought autumn ambience to western Washington and Oregon, while mountainous areas near the coast remained above the pall. The post Cloudy Cloak Over the Northwest appeared first on NASA Science .
